note: PEEK_S reads 2 bytes from s->iseq+pos0. If pos0 points to the last byte of the iseq buffer, this causes a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.
JMPLINK_START is 0xffff. If pos0 is not JMPLINK_START, the code proceeds to read the jump target from the iseq buffer.
If newpos is 0, the jump is resolved and both bytes are zeroed out.
If newpos is non-zero, the jump target is written back to the iseq buffer.
pos1 is computed as pos0 plus the jump offset. If newpos is an absolute position (not an offset), pos1 can point beyond the iseq buffer.
If pos1 equals pos0, the jump is self-referential and dispatch returns.

code: if (pos1 > s->pc) { codegen_error(s, "jump target out of range"); }
note: If pos1 exceeds the current program counter, a codegen error is raised. This check may not catch all OOB cases if pos1 is within the allocated buffer but beyond the valid iseq length.
Recursive call to dispatch with the computed pos1. If pos1 points to the last byte of the iseq buffer, the recursive call will trigger the OOB read.

When the argument a exceeds 0xff (255), genjmp2 writes the absolute program counter pc instead of a relative offset. This causes dispatch() to compute pos1 = pos0 + pc, which can be far beyond the iseq buffer.
When a <= 0xff, the value a is written as the jump offset. The vulnerability occurs only when a > 0xff and pc != JMPLINK_START.
If pc is not JMPLINK_START, the OP_JMP opcode is written at position pc. The jump target is stored at pc+1 and pc+2.
Returns the position pc where the jump instruction was written. This position is later used by dispatch() to resolve the jump chain.
If pc is JMPLINK_START, the function returns immediately without writing anything.
Writes the OP_JMP opcode at position pc in the iseq buffer.
Writes the current program counter s->pc as the jump target. This is an absolute position, not a relative offset.
Iterates through the jump chain, calling dispatch() for each position. If dispatch() returns a position beyond the iseq buffer, the loop continues and triggers the OOB read.
Returns the final position after the jump chain is resolved.

The vulnerability is triggered when s->sp (stack pointer) exceeds 255, causing genjmp2 to write an absolute position instead of a relative offset. This requires more than 255 local variables or stack values.

The compiler limits local variables to 255 (0xff). With 254 user locals plus 1 for self, s->nlocals = 255. Adding a case statement pushes the case value onto the stack, making s->sp = 256, which exceeds 255.
The OOB read occurs when pos0 points to the last byte of the iseq buffer. PEEK_S reads 2 bytes, but only 1 byte is available, causing a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.
